設.meaning: A <part>maiden</part> gives a rousing <part>speech</part> in an empty field, and as she talks, tents pop up, wells get dug and a bakery appears. By sunset every traveller has a bed, bread and water. She made <kanji>provision</kanji> for all.
設.on: A red <sound>set</sound>ter trots between the tents, handing out blankets from a basket in its mouth.
設.kun: Last of all she sets up a shed for the lawn<sound>mow</sound>er, to keep the campsite grass short.

置.meaning: A fisherman lowers his <part>net</part> onto the sand and lays each shell inside it in one <part>straight</part> line, checking with a ruler. Not a millimetre out of line. He fusses for hours over the <kanji>placement</kanji> of every one.
置.on: A <sound>chee</sound>tah sneaks up behind him and nudges one shell out of line, just to annoy him.
置.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' he groans, and puts it back exactly where it was.

演.meaning: In front of a tiny <part>shrine</part>, a frog in a velvet cape bows, then leaps through the <part>water drops</part> falling from the eaves while juggling three pebbles. A crowd of snails gasps and claps. What a <kanji>performance</kanji>!
演.on: For the finale he rides a toy steam <sound>en</sound>gine round the shrine, whistle blowing.

独.meaning: On a long <part>fishhook</part> dangles one lonely <part>insect</part>, the only bait in the whole lake. Shoals of fish swim past in a crowd, but nobody keeps it company. Just one bug, all by itself: <kanji>single</kanji>.
独.on: The fisherman has fallen asleep at the end of the empty <sound>dock</sound>, rod still in hand.
独.kun: The bug taps one <sound>hee</sound>l on the hook, then climbs to the <sound>to</sound>p of the line, alone.

申.meaning: A <part>pole</part> pierces the <part>sun</part> top to bottom, like a giant sundial pin. When its shadow touches the teacups painted on the town square, everyone stops for tea and cake, until the shadow reaches the dinner plates. That's the slot from <kanji>3-5PM</kanji>.
申.on: Every day at three, a waiter trips over the pole and bangs his <sound>shin</sound>, spilling the tea.
申.kun: Every day at five, a man on a <sound>mow</sound>er rides through the square and humbly says tea is over.

寄.meaning: On a dark night, something <part>strange</part> glows on your <part>roof</part>: a little green light, humming to itself. Every cat in the street creeps closer, then closer still, whiskers trembling. They just can't help but <kanji>draw near</kanji>.
寄.on: It's a lost brass <sound>key</sound>, floating and glowing, and the cats want to know which door it opens.
寄.kun: On their way home they stop in at your kitchen for a lick of <sound>yo</sound>gurt.

極.meaning: A <part>vise</part> clamps a <part>tree</part> and squeezes it tighter and tighter until its rings pop and sap squirts out like toothpaste. Bolts groan, the workbench bends, the floor cracks. This is squeezing taken to the <kanji>extreme</kanji>.
極.on: The sap oozes down the bench like a stic<sound>ky</sound> <sound>yolk</sound>.
極.kun: A <sound>ki</sound>wi bird hops onto the handle and cranks it one last notch: '<sound>Wah</sound>!'

異.meaning: Above a <part>rice field</part>, the scarecrows stand <part>together</part> in neat rows: identical straw hats, identical frowns. But one of them wears a pink tutu and is doing a handstand. Now that's <kanji>uncommon</kanji>.
異.on: Even odder, an <sound>ee</sound>l is wrapped round its ankle like a sock.
異.kun: At night it sleeps on a <sound>co</sound>t on <sound>to</sound>p of the barn, not out in the field like all the rest.

説.meaning: A little horned <part>imp</part> climbs onto an upturned bucket and gives a long <part>speech</part> about why socks should be worn on the ears. Nobody asked, and he won't stop. Well, everyone's entitled to an <kanji>opinion</kanji>.
説.on: His only fan is a red <sound>set</sound>ter, wagging its tail with a sock on each ear.
説.kun: He climbs to the <sound>to</sound>p of the bucket and explains it all over again, louder.
